item.title: [CPM-639] Icon Color Extraction to be improved
item.description:
We have this case:

This icon seems green but is marked as black. also all 3 instances “black” seem to be the same exact color.

We’ll attach other cases if we find them but this seems odd at least.
item.summary: Icon Color Extraction to be improved

status.description: This status is managed internally by Jira

comments.comment:
AdrianValentin Tomita translating specific inks to Names and to RGB (web) colors is always a bit of science mixed with a bit of art mixed with a bit of hocus pocus.

These “greenish” colors are being reported as Black because they have low HSL brightness. With this low brightness, the hue is never being considered.

So I’ve changed this to consider “Saturation” as well, based on some suggestions from Claude. With that in place, the file in question would have reported 1 instance of White and three instances of a very-similar-but-technically-different “Cyan.”

“Why not green?” you ask?

At ~161°, your color falls into the 135–195 range, which is mapped to "Cyan". That is technically correct in HSL terms — (0, 71, 49) is a dark blue-green/teal, which sits closer to cyan than pure green on the color wheel (pure green is 120°).

This is on DEV for review. Note that while I reprocessed this one icon to show the before/after differences, other icons would not be reprocessed without intervention or a future update to the icon file.

item.title: [CPM-555] Icon Family Change Management (OU-Region Logic)
item.description:
As indicated in the UI changes explained in https://jira-pg.atlassian.net/browse/CPM-369, we need to be able to assign OUs and Regions to Families, and that data must flow to Enovia.

We can use 1 new field to send that information (FamilyAttributes) and have them be sent like Fabric Care, EUROPE ENTERPRISE; Oral Care, EUROPE ENTERPRISE. → To validate with Tripo/Jyoti how this data must flow.

Stephen Ferda to provide some icon output json (update to enovia) so that we can modify it to expectations.

One Icon can be rep for only one family.

Current assumption: Both Icons, and Families, can have multiple OUs assigned, but when it comes to Regions, they will either be single region, or be global (all existing regions assigned). This will be controlled by the process, by letting the icon-uploader team and the OUs to not use multi region icons unless they’re global.

The reason why we need this logic is to allow the following scenarios:

BC1 (Case 1)

I have a FC NA icon, version 1, released.

BC1-CM1 (Case 1, Scenario 1)

If I add it to a family (FamilyName1) that is assigned to FC NA, the icon will be up versioned to version 2, and released immediately (without approval process). When doing so, the newer version is part of a family, but is not family rep, so we don’t send update to Enovia about v2, but we’ll send them update about v1 being obsoleted (and set validity date to yesterday).

BC2-CM2

If I add it to a family (FamilyName1) that is assigned to FC NA, and the icon is set as REP to that family, the icon will be up versioned to version 2, and released immediately (without approval process). When doing so, because Icon is rep, we send update to Enovia about v2 being released, and also about v1 being obsolete (and set validity date to yesterday).

BC2

I have an icon that is assigned to both FC NA and OC NA.

BC2-CM1

I’m adding this Icon to a family that is assigned to FC NA (FamilyName1). Since this icon is not a rep for that family, Enovia doesn’t need to create a clone for FC NA of that icon, as they will just use the Rep for that. However, they need to have a standalone icon for OC NA. To allow that, we will use subtraction logic.

Icon: FC NA, OC NA, not REP of FamilyName1.

FamilyName1: FC NA

Icon_data_sent_to_enovia: OC NA (hiding FC NA, and family name)

BC2-CM2

I’m adding this icon to FamilyName1 (owned by FC NA), but i’m also setting it as the Rep for that family.

Enovia will need a clone for FC NA that is rep, a clone for OC NA that is not part of family. They will apply that logic on their end. We’ll just give them the full information of the icon, and they will use the attributes in the family to determine which clones they need to create or not.

Still obsoleting version 1, and setting validity date to yesterday.

BC3

I have an icon that is assigned to OC NA and FC NA, part of FamilyName1 (owned by FC NA) so Enovia only sees the data for OC NA (and no family assigned) as Icon is not the rep of FamilyName1.

BC3-CM1

If I assign the icon as Family Rep for FamilyName1, I’ll obsolete version 1, release version 2 as rep, and send both the data for OC NA, FC NA, and family to Enovia. They will need to make sure on their end that the OC NA clone is not part of a family, but the FC NA clone is.

BC3-CM2

If I also assign the icon to FamilyName2 (owned by OC NA), by the subtraction logic, Enovia no longer sees the icon, as it’s only available for FC NA and OC NA, and for both OUs the icon is in a family, but is not a rep for any of the families.

This means that we must obsolete the existing v1, create and release v2, but v2 won’t be sent to Enovia, as they will use the Reps of those 2 families.

BC3-CM3

If I remove the icon from FamilyName1, I will obsolete it and change validity date, and release v2, with all the data assigned to it as it’s no longer part of any family.

BC4

Icon is FC NA, OC NA, and is rep of FamilyName1 (owned by FC NA).

BC4-CM1

I remove it as a rep

BC4-CM2

I remove it from the family

BC5

Icon in 2 families, not rep

BC5-CM1

I move icon from one of the families to another family.

BC6

Icon in 2 families, Rep of Both → Not possible

BC7

Icon in 2 families, Rep of One,

BC7-CM1

Changing one of families, that icon is not rep of.

BC8

Icon is in 1 family, owned by both OUs (FC NA, OC NA)

BC8-CM1

We modify family to remove 1 OU

BC9

Icon in 2 OU, Family Rep in FamilyName1 (Owned by FC NA)

BC9-CM1

We modify family to remove 1 OU

BC10

Icon is in family owned by 1 OU

BC10-CM1

We modify family to add 1 OU

item.title: [CPM-521] Create new version with same graphic
item.description:
When we create a new version, we are forced to upload a new graphic (or reupload the same one).

New version should be created without requesting new icon, but new icon can be provided.

If it’s not provided, reuse the graphic of the previous version.

2 Scenarios:

  1. If new version is created without uploading new graphic, the canonical and graphic ID will stay the same, but the version will increase by 1.
  2. If new version is created by also uploading a new graphic, the canonical ID stays the same, the graphic ID changes, and the version will increate by 1.
item.summary: Create new version with same graphic

comments.comment:
AdrianValentin Tomita I suspect there is a bit of misunderstanding as to what these various “IDs” represent.

  1. The Canonical ID is the authoritative Id shared by the entire “lineage” of an icon from version 1 through version N. It does not change.
  2. The Unique Graphic Id represents a version of an Icon. The version represented by an asset with a given Unique Graphic Id contains all the unique metadata about that version. A new Unique Graphic Id is generated with each version – it is the incrementing database primary key for that row.

So keeping the Unique Graphic Id the same across different versions is probably not going to be an easy task without inventing new Id-like structures.

There is one other Id which is not displayed in the UI anywhere: the AssetFileId. This is the Id of the actual binary asset (generally a PDF) which is associated with a version of an Icon. (It can be shared by completely different Icons, technically, but that is pretty unusual.)

So…

  1. We could allow a new version to reuse the same icon as the previous version, but keep displaying the newly-generated Unique Graphic Id as before.
  2. We could allow a new version to reuse the same icon as the previous version, but we could change what we currently display in the Unique Graphic Id spot to, instead, be the AssetFileId.

#1 is simplest and likely has the fewest risks. It is also closest to what is probably already happening today… You make a New Version, upload the same PDF again, and the system is already hashing, comparing, and throwing out the duplicate. Change #1 would just eliminate the need to upload the asset again.

Thoughts?

Stephen Ferda I get the point, but can’t we have a composite primary key for the DB using Canonical & Version? Regardless of Unique Graphic ID Changes, (Canonical + Version) will be sufficient to determine an exact icon version.

For AssetID, as long as it points to the actual file, which as we said might or might not change from a version to another, we might be able to use it, but it should then replace the graphic ID in the UI completely, while also still using the Graphic ID name. This however wasn’t aligned as the way to go so I’d have to go back and get approval for this specific route

AdrianValentin Tomita I’m not sure what to do next. The simplest solution which seems consistent with your comment is to change this to read Unique Graphic Id 764v4 instead of displaying the underlying GraphicElementId of 1022. Do you agree?

Stephen Ferda No, that’s not it. To give you some context on why we need a graphical id that only changes when the icon changes, and not the metadata:

We might update an icon version 3-4 times before time actually comes to update the actual graphic.

For any change we make, the studio team must take into account the new icon, download it, and check if there are differences in the actual icon graphic. If the graphic ID only changed when we changed the actual graphic, this would save them a lot of trouble. If the graphic ID was “canonical”+”version” then it would change with every version.

I was suggesting “764v4” as a candidate for DB composite primary key, not as graphic ID, so we could free the “unique graphic id” from it’s duty as DB primary key.

If that causes too much trouble, you may use the AssetID as the Unique Graphic ID (it must still display as Unique Graphic ID and the message we send to Enovia shouldn’t change), but again, to make sure, it must only change with actual icon graphic changes, not version changes that rely purely on metadata. And we must make sure that the system is not forcing us to upload new icon (as it’s currently doing that) when we create a new version.

AdrianValentin Tomita

The simplest way forward, I think, is to display the id for the actual binary asset in place of "Unique Graphic Id." This is the number that represents the essence of what you're trying to communicate, I think.

This number is already in the JSON; it's here

There are three "Id-like" entities at work...

  1. CanonicalId – the Id shared by all members of an Icon's lineage.
  2. GraphicElementId – the Id for a specific version of a metadata set.
  3. AssetId – The Id for a specific binary

Can I fulfill the requirements of this card by changing the UI to display the AssetId?

item.title: [CPM-508] Basic Duplicate Detection
item.description:
Using the duplicate detection algorithm that has the “cropping” feature (to counter wrong alignment of icon) we need to ensure that the icons being uploaded don’t have duplicates on icondb, but also that the uploader is not trying to upload 1 or more duplicates within the bulk upload batch.

Just 2 error types for starters.

For duplicate on system

  1. Icon X (to replace with icon description) already exists in the system as “canonical” “icon id” (and a link that opens in a new tab → going to the existing icon so bpx team can update it)

For duplicate on batch

  1. Icon X (to replace with icon description) is duplicate of Icon Y (to replace with icon description) & Icon ID

(and a link that opens in a new tab → going to the existing icon so bpx team can update it)

comments.comment:
AdrianValentin Tomita we should probably talk this through.

The duplicate checking algo is currently using pHash. (Other options are dHash and aHash, but for the most part, they are similar.) This is not a firm determination of an exact match. It’s an approximate calculation of how “close” one images is to another. If it is within a certain threshold of “closeness,” we can guess that it might be a duplicate of an existing icon. But we cannot tell that FOR SURE using this algorithm.

On DEV right now is one approach to this.

The user is encouraged, but not required, to review existing “close matches” to decide if they should continue uploading this icon.

Originally, we hard-stopped the attempt to upload an image which was a “close match.” But if an icon has genuine-but-subtle differences, it risks getting blocked from uploading with no way to override the system. So at present, it is an optional check. We can always go back to hard-stop, but it will raise management issues down the road.

Now, the bulk upload is an even nastier version of this issue. There is not an elegant way to give the user any feedback on a “close match” before it is too late and the asset would have already been added to the system. We could do a literal hash of the binary of the PDF and block those, but that doesn’t seem terribly useful – we already discard literal binary matches on PDFs in favor of associating them to the existing PDF. We could decide to report “close matches” on screen during the initial stage of import, but then we would need to develop some way of doing something with those close matches, and that is presently out of the scope of this card. (At one point, Rachel or maybe you had mocked up a big set of screens to deal with this, if I recall correctly.)

Thoughts on all of this?

Stephen Ferda We did briefly test the algorithm with an exact duplicate and we noticed the following: The check is visible, and seems to pick on duplicates correctly, however:

-It only triggers / gives response when doing upload via “New graphic” button.

-It does not prevent the icon from being uploaded.

-On bulk upload (where this feature is really needed most) it just goes through, no error, no notice of duplicates.

item.description:

Attributes to force new version include:

  • Name
  • Type
  • Category / Subcategory / Brand
  • Region
  • Market
  • Icon Family
  • SubCopy Type
  • Package Level

Attributes that can’t be edited anymore after the icon’s first version becomes released:

  • Copy Integration Type

The exceptions are:

  • Validity date: this doesn’t need to trigger a new version and we should be able to edit it on any icon. (if we have write access)

Findings based on our call…

  1. “Why don’t the Regions change in IconDB when I make a change in the backend?”
    At present, there is a relatively-short-term memory cache on Regions. This is for performance reasons and because, until quite recently, Regions basically never changed. I cycled the memory on the IconDB application, and now the Regions display as intended. If Regions are expected to change more frequently in the future, we will need a cache-buster change for this.
  1. “Where do the Regions in IconDB come from? Is it the same list as in Rules Manager?”
    Regions in IconDB are housed in the table [dLabs].[Region] which is the Canvas table for Region data.  Canvas’ list of Markets use this Region data, but a great many of those entries are set to the Region “Unknown.”

Regions in the Lookup Cluster tool for Touchless are likewise housed in the table [dLabs].[Region].

Regions in Rules Manager are housed in the table rules.PackageTriggerValue which is the main key-value-pair table for PackageTrigger data in Rules Manager.  They have no database-managed relationship with Markets whatsoever, nor do they have a relationship with dlabs.Region.

Regions in AQIQ derive from report data submitted to AQIQ. It is stored as string data within the [AQIQ].[tPoa] table. It has no relationship between either the Canvas list of Regions nor the Rules Manager list of Regions.

I’m not familiar with the “Lookup Cluster tool for Touchless”, but would it make sense that both used “rules.PackageTriggerValue” instead of [dLabs].[Region]?
